active_themes.label: AI Spending Backlash
active_themes.summary: The relief that followed Nvidia's earnings has been erased. The Nasdaq fell 2.25% to 23,879 and the VIX rose to 28.44. Anthropic's record IPO closed its first day at $97, and the new supply of AI stock is a likely extra source of selling pressure. The open question is whether the market treats this as digestion or as a re-pricing of AI valuations.

active_themes.label: Global Borrowing Costs Climb
active_themes.summary: The 10-year yield edged down 0.01 points to 5.05% and the 30-year to 5.40% even as stocks sold off hard. Long-term yields are high but holding rather than climbing. The open question is whether the 10-year breaks below 5.00% or climbs toward 5.25%.

active_themes.label: Fed Eyes Another Hike
active_themes.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller's half-point hike idea remains unechoed by any other policymaker. Goolsbee's inflation warning adds a second voice on the hawkish side of the inflation argument, though he did not call for a specific move. The open question is whether another official endorses a half-point hike before December.

active_themes.label: AI Drives Inflation
active_themes.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called AI-linked inflation 'disturbingly high', pointing to the data-center construction boom. IMF head Kristalina Georgieva warned AI demand will push interest rates up worldwide. This breaks the older hope that AI would be a disinflationary productivity story. The open question is whether bond yields start to confirm it, with the 10-year at 5.05% today.

active_themes.label: Gulf Oil Slowly Returns
active_themes.summary: Brent fell 1.28% to $91.95 and WTI 3.2% to $83.26, even after a Houthi strike on a Saudi wealth-fund tower in Riyadh. Oil is shrugging off attacks that do not cut actual supply. The open question is whether Brent stays under $95 if a strike hits shipping or output.

active_themes.label: Iran War Resumption Risk
active_themes.summary: Iran fired at Kuwait after a US strike on an Iranian island, a fresh escalation. Brent rose only 0.76% to $93.14, below the $95 line, so the market is not yet pricing a real loss of supply. The open question is whether further strikes push Brent back above $95 and toward $100.

That would mark a shift from nervous caution to genuine panic, the kind of regime where forced selling feeds on itself.
Hike expectations are still building and gold and stocks face more pressure from a stronger dollar.
The hawkish shock is fading and the hedging trade is stabilizing.

open_watchlist.condition: A Fed policymaker other than Waller publicly says a half-point hike is warranted.
open_watchlist.meaning: The outsized hike is a committee idea and not one governor's trial balloon, so December hike risk rises sharply.
Cheaper fuel is starting to take pressure off inflation, which weakens the case for a big hike.
The AI-drives-rates argument would have bond-market confirmation, which is the sharpest pressure on high-priced tech shares.
Demand for AI stock itself would be fading, so the IPO stops being a side effect and becomes a signal.
Investors would still be liquidating even safe-haven assets to raise cash, which points to forced selling that has not run its course.
